Prelaunch.metaTitle: Ruta Opta · Talent and community tourism in Colombia
Prelaunch.metaDescription: A route to recognize the talent of rural families in six territories of Colombia and connect it with opportunities. In progress.
Prelaunch.ogAlt: Ruta Opta: “The talent in communities can transform their territories”, over a paper-relief coffee valley with the Ruta Opta sun.
Prelaunch.ogTitle: The talent in communities can transform their territories
Prelaunch.ogDescription: A route in progress to recognize the talent of rural families and connect it with opportunities.
Prelaunch.title: The talent in communities can transform their territories.
Prelaunch.lead: We are designing a route for rural families in six territories of Colombia to recognize their talents and turn them into opportunities. We will start with the 12 municipalities of Quindío. We have not opened yet.

thesis.title: Why Ruta Opta exists
thesis.text: Ruta Opta was born after the earthquake of 10 August 2026. Stephania Forero, legal representative of Fundación Embajadores de la Paz, had spent years visiting rural communities and had seen a great deal of talent without tools. She decided to leave behind “isolated interventions” and build a route that connects that talent with opportunities.
thesis.stance: Each territory decides its own path; no route should get communities used to others deciding for them.
thesis.commitmentsLabel: Four commitments on how we will work

listen.title: Listen first
listen.text: Every cycle starts with meetings with the mayor's office, leaders and families, and with written agreements.

recognize.title: Recognize
recognize.text: Each person builds their own map of strengths.

connect.title: Connect with care
connect.text: An experience is offered only after it has been validated with the host family and with allies.

decide.title: Decide together
decide.text: The community can accept, change or turn down any activity.

Prelaunch.methodTitle: Grow, create, connect: a path in three steps

grow.name: Grow
grow.tagline: Recognize who I am, what I feel and what I can contribute.
grow.text: Eight weeks of meetings to recognize what each person feels, knows and can contribute. By the end, each participant builds their own map of strengths.

create.name: Create
create.tagline: Turn knowledge and talents into proposals.
create.text: Ten weeks to recover the memory of the territory (recipes, crafts, places) and turn knowledge into proposals, with costs, a price and a presentation.

connect.name: Connect
connect.tagline: Present proposals to the people who can buy and support them.
connect.text: Six weeks to validate each proposal and present it to allies and visitors.

tourism.title: Turismo Vivo: rural experiences designed by the people who live there
tourism.text: A possibility, not a promise to every family: we only design an experience where the community is interested, safety conditions are met and the requirements are in order. A meal, a walk, a craft, told by the people who live it.

places.title: Six territories, one route
places.lead: In every territory we start by listening to those who govern and live in it, in their own ways of deciding: mayors' offices, community action boards and families.
places.quindio: A detailed 36-month plan across its 12 municipalities: Armenia, Buenavista, Calarcá, Circasia, Córdoba, Filandia, Génova, La Tebaida, Montenegro, Pijao, Quimbaya and Salento.

what.q: What is Ruta Opta, and what is it not?
what.a: A training and support route that starts from people's talent, driven by Fundación Embajadores de la Paz. It complements the work of the State; it does not replace it in health, housing or protection.

book.q: Can I book an experience yet?
book.a: Not yet. Turismo Vivo is in progress. Leave us your email and we will let you know when it opens.

allies.q: How can I become an ally?
allies.a: Pick the way that best matches you (train, coordinate, validate, drive, accompany or share) and write to us on WhatsApp or at info@rutaopta.org. Tell us who you are, what you can contribute and in which territory.

data.q: What do you do with my data?
data.a: We use your name and email only to send you Ruta Opta news and to let you know when we open. You can unsubscribe at any time from any email. The details are in our data processing policy.

when.a: There is no public date yet. People on the list hear first.

donate.a: Not yet. First we need the process, the reports and the protection protocols in place. If you would like to partner with a specific contribution, write to us.

Privacy.title: Data protection policy
Privacy.intro: This policy explains what data Ruta Opta collects on its website and its waitlist, what we use it for and how you can exercise your rights.
Privacy.effective: In effect since 25 November 2026. The waitlist database stays in effect for as long as Ruta Opta sends news. Once a year we will email you to remind you, and you can unsubscribe from that email.

controller.title: Data controller
controller.text: Fundación Embajadores de la Paz, responsible for Ruta Opta, NIT 901679710-4, based at Carrera 13 #2N-49, Torre Fundadores 202, Armenia, Quindío. Legal representative: Stephania Forero. Phone: +57 310 587 4657. Email: privacy@rutaopta.org.

data.title: What data we ask for
data.text: For the waitlist we ask for your name and your email address. If you came through one of our links, such as the one on Instagram, we also note which one. We keep them until you unsubscribe; after that we keep them only so we never email you again.

purpose.title: What we use it for
purpose.text: We use your name and email to send you news from Ruta Opta and let you know when we open. We use the link you came through only to count how many people sign up from each one. We don't use this data for anything else.

measurement.title: How we measure visits
measurement.text:
We use Plausible Analytics to know how many people visit the site, where they come from and which buttons they use. The measurement uses no cookies and stores nothing on your phone or computer. It records the page you open, the site or link you came from, the contact and sign-up buttons and links you tap, how long you stay and how far you scroll, your device type, system and browser, and your approximate country, region and city. So that it doesn't count you twice on the same day, it creates a code from your IP address and browser details. The code changes every day and your IP address is not stored. We don't send it your name, your email or anything you type in the form.

Apart from measurement, the site may set one cookie to remember the language you are reading it in. It is temporary, holds only "es" or "en", and is not used for measurement.

contact.title: If you write to us by WhatsApp or email
contact.text: If you write to us on WhatsApp or at info@rutaopta.org, for example to become an ally, we use what you tell us (your name, your organization and your message) only to reply and to talk with you about that collaboration. WhatsApp, from Meta, and your email provider process those messages under their own terms. You can ask us to delete the conversation by writing to privacy@rutaopta.org.

processor.title: Who helps us
processor.text: We send newsletters with Zoho Campaigns and confirmation emails with Zoho CPaaS, both from Zoho Corporation. The site is hosted on Netlify. Visit data passes through Netlify and is processed by Plausible Insights OÜ, a company in Estonia that stores it on servers in the European Union. These providers may store data on servers outside Colombia.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.text: You can see, update and correct your data, ask us to delete it and withdraw your authorization. You can also ask for proof of the authorization you gave us, ask what we have used your data for and access it free of charge. To stop receiving emails, use the unsubscribe link in any of them.

requests.title: How to exercise your rights
requests.text:
Stephania Forero, legal representative, handles requests, queries and claims about your data. Write to privacy@rutaopta.org with your name, the email address you signed up with and what you need.

A query is how you find out what data we hold and how we use it. We answer it within 10 business days at most. If we can't, we will tell you why and on what date we will answer, which will be no more than 5 business days after that deadline.

A claim is how you correct, update or delete data, withdraw your authorization or tell us about a breach of the law. Tell us what happened, give us a contact address and attach any documents you want us to review. If information is missing, we ask for it within 5 days. If 2 months pass without it, we take it that you dropped the claim. We answer within 15 business days at most, counted from the day after we receive it. If we can't, we will tell you why and on what date we will answer, which will be no more than 8 business days after that deadline.

You can file a complaint with the Superintendence of Industry and Commerce (Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio) after going through this procedure with us.
